title: feat(security): the external organization role is the EXTERNAL principal — owner-only org-wide default, explicit grants only
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoFqCf6db2fM7iSSM3dJb5rf)_

Closes #25233

Stage 2 of the ruling of record 6355206139, letter B (item 2, with the scope note 6371125645). Stage 1 landed in #25515. The Tier H ADR text follows in its own docs PR once this lands.

Clause-②: yes (widening: `@objectstack/core` gains `owdForAudience`, `isExternalAudienceContext`, `externalGrantSpeaks` and the two grant-stamp keys; every narrowing below applies only to the `external` role, which no release has shipped yet)
Metadata-protocol: semantic

## What this does

A holder of the `external` organization role is now the EXTERNAL principal. It reaches rows through explicit grants only: shares (share links included), sharing rules, and the position and permission-set grants it holds, with their RLS evaluated. The internal org-wide default never widens it.

| Item | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| audience and posture | `core` `resolve-authz-context.ts`, `posture-ladder.ts`, `assemble-execution-context.ts` | The resolver stamps `audience: 'external'` on a holder and `derivePosture` returns `EXTERNAL`. Precedence is PLATFORM_ADMIN, then EXTERNAL, then TENANT_ADMIN, then MEMBER. The assembled context carries the audience, on agent envelopes too. `POSTURE_INJECTION_RULE.EXTERNAL` states the channel list. |
| OWD seam | `core` `external-owd-floor.ts`; `plugin-sharing` `sharing-service.ts` | `owdForAudience` floors an external's effective model to `private` (owner plus shares) in `buildReadFilter`, `buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit` and `checkDelete`. The floor lifts for one object and one operation class when plugin-security has stamped that a held grant's RLS speaks for it. |
| grant stamp | `plugin-security` `external-owd-grant-stamp.ts`, `security-plugin.ts` step 2.6, `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts` | For an external, `__externalReadGrant` / `__externalWriteGrant` hold the object name when a held set's `using` policy applies (the write class follows Layer 1's select-derives-write rule). The object's declared default row scope and the platform ownership floor are not grants. The keys are operation-private, and a stamp naming another object reads as no grant. |
| write floor | `plugin-security` `default-permission-sets.ts` | `external_default` carries `owner_only_writes` and `owner_only_deletes`, bound to `org_external`. They share the member floor's provenance key, so every relief of a member's floor relieves an external's. Without it an external's write reach on a public object was org-wide, wider than a member's (I2). |
| access matrix | `plugin-security` `authz-matrix-gate.test.ts` | The EXTERNAL column, at Layers 0 and 1 (the sharing floor is pinned in plugin-sharing): on `task` the external reads in-org rows its grant opens and writes only rows it created; `private_obj` and `platform_global` are denied; on `better_auth` it reads and writes its own row only. The ladder order includes it. |
| explain and describe | `plugin-security` `explain-engine.ts`, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`, `security-plugin.ts` | Explain and describe resolve the baseline the principal actually gets (`humanBaselineFor`), so an external's is `external_default`, attributed as "external baseline (org_external)". The OWD layer reports "owner_only for an external principal" when no held grant speaks, using the same predicate as the stamp. |
| directory doors | `plugin-auth` `external-directory-door.ts`, `auth-manager.ts` | `list-teams` and `get-full-organization`'s `teams` answer an external only the teams it sits on (read from `sys_team_member`). `list-invitations` answers it only invitations to its own email. The door docblock notes that the resolver uses `includes('external')` while the door requires exactly `'external'`, which E5 makes the same population. |
| spec prose | `spec` `execution-context.zod.ts`, `explain.zod.ts` | The `audience` docblock and the EXTERNAL posture description name the channels. Generated reference docs are regenerated. |

Measured for the scope note: better-auth 1.7.12's `listInvitations` (`crud-invites.mjs`) checks membership only and returns every invitation of the organization, so it is narrowed. `listOrganizationTeams` and get-full-organization's `teams` (with `teams.enabled`, set in `auth-manager.ts`) check membership only too.

## Acceptance notes

On a real showcase boot, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-member-directory.dogfood.test.ts` adds five stage 2 cases (11/11 pass):

- **The OWD baseline never widens an external.** On `showcase_announcement` (`public_read`), the external with a plain read grant gets exactly its own row and the row shared to it, out of four.
- **A held grant's RLS lifts the floor and bounds the rows.** A second external holds a read grant with `title == '<portal title>'` as its select policy. It gets exactly the one matching row, which it neither owns nor was shared.
- **Teams.** `list-teams` and get-full-organization's `teams` answer the external only the team it sits on. An external on no team gets `[]`.
- **Invitations.** `list-invitations` answers the external only the invitation to its own email. Another external gets `[]`.

Armed controls: the member reads all four fixture rows, and the member is answered both teams and both invitations.

Unit pins:

- `core` `posture-ladder.test.ts` (EXTERNAL ⊆ MEMBER with the new grant row, the injection rule, and derivation precedence), `external-owd-floor.test.ts` (6), the resolver's external-population audience and posture cells, and assembly audience carriage.
- `plugin-sharing` `external-owd-floor.test.ts` (15): reads and writes on every public model, stamp scoping by object and class, ownerless objects, and member controls.
- `plugin-security` `external-owd-grant-stamp.test.ts` (9), `explain-external-principal.test.ts` (6), and the matrix's EXTERNAL column with an end-to-end stamp check.
- `plugin-auth` `external-directory-door.test.ts` (teams, full-org teams and invitations, with member controls).

Existing pins moved deliberately:

- `platform-ownership-policies.test.ts` now deduplicates the floor by its identity key. The floor has two carriers, `member_default` and `external_default`, and a new case pins exactly those two.

Notes for review:

- **Clause-②:** for an external holder this is a narrowing (no OWD widening, the write floor, and the narrowed doors), but stage 1's `external` role has not shipped in a release yet: its changeset is still pending in `.changeset/`. No principal without the role changes.
- **Fix after the first review (225d5bc02):** the floor no longer applies to a `controlled_by_parent` detail. Its rows follow the master (ADR-0055), and the master already meets the floor. Before the fix, an external who was shared a master read none of its lines. `plugin-sharing`'s `external-owd-floor.test.ts` had pinned that wrong answer, and the first contract review (6375883728) passed it. The fix is `owdForPrincipal` in `sharing-service.ts` and the same exemption in explain's OWD layer. A showcase dogfood case pins it: `showcase_invoice` is shared to an external, who reads its two `showcase_invoice_line` rows and not the other invoice's. The case is red with the exemption removed (measured) and green with it. The merge of main (c70863feb) also resolved the conflict with #25536, which moved the after-hook.
- **Reading of "access matrix":** I took it as the EXTERNAL role column of `authz-matrix-gate`. ADR-0090 D11 also mentions a "D6 access matrix external-audience column", which is the explain matrix. If that was meant, it is a follow-up.
- **Out of scope, found while measuring:** a share on an object whose effective model is `public` (`public_read_write`, `controlled_by_parent`, or a model-less system object) is refused at create as "inert" (`inertGrantReason`; `public_read` is not refused). Now that such an object is owner-only for an external, a share to an external there is no longer inert, so the create gate, which also runs for sharing-rule materialisation, closes those two channels on that set of objects. Existing rows are honoured, and the direction is fail-closed. This needs its own card and a ruling (contract review 6375883728).
- **#25234 PR ②** also touches plugin-security. Whichever lands second merges main.

Verification: the plugin-security (4602), core (2806), plugin-sharing (1224), plugin-auth (3620), plugin-approvals (1233) and rest (6608) suites pass. They ran before the merge of main, which touched only plugin-auth among these packages; after it, plugin-auth's `tsc` and its external door and membership tests (37) re-pass. `tsc` is clean for core, plugin-security (including the test program), plugin-sharing, plugin-auth and dogfood. All 121 derived gates were run and reconciled with `dispatch-gates --ran` (0 not measured). The diff is 1543 insertions and 142 deletions across 35 files.
